sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x bibliography for kutt1236 (title search 'Kupto'; author search 'Leger', 'Zoch') and Google Books full-text snippet queries (Kupto + Akzent/Betonung/stress/accent/tone).
sources.note: No snippet anywhere pairs Kupto with stress/accent/Akzent/Betonung; all Kupto snippets concern lexicon, gender, pronouns, tone levelling.

sources.citation: Baldi, Sergio & Rudolf Leger. 2020. Innovative features of nouns and pronouns in Chadic languages of the Nigerian Gongola-Benue basin. In N. Pawlak & I. Will (eds.), West African languages. Linguistic theory and communication, 46-56. Warsaw: WUW. DOI 10.31338/uw.9788323546313.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p.47 states that in the northern Bole-Tangale languages (Bole, Kwami, Kupto, Maha) 'the flexibility of tone plays an important role in the grammar', versus tone levelling to low in the southern languages; refers the reader to Leger 2014:230-234 for phonology/tonology.

sources.citation: Downing, Laura J. 2004. What African languages tell us about accent typology. ZAS Papers in Linguistics 37: 101-136.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Kupto. p.109 reports Leger (1994:91-92) describing word stress in the sister language Kwami (long-vowel syllables stressed; else initial H-toned or closed syllable; else final) -- evidence that Leger records accent in his Bole-Tangale descriptions, hence the list of works to obtain priority on his Kupto works.

sources.citation: Dinslage, Sabine & Rudolf Leger. 1996. Language and migration: the impact of the Jukun on Chadic speaking groups in the Benue-Gongola basin. Berichte des SFB 268, Bd. 8: 67-75.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; historical/ethnolinguistic. Useful only for its bibliography (Leger 1991 FAB 3 'Grammatische Analyse einer Herkunftserzählung der Kupto').

sources.citation: Jungraithmayr, Herrmann & Rudolf Leger. 1993. The Benue-Gongola-Chad Basin: zone of ethnic and linguistic compression. Berichte des Sonderforschungsbereichs 268, Bd. 2: 161-173. Frankfurt a.M.: SFB 268.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Section '1. The sound system' (p.166) gives Kupto a 5-vowel system with tone-marked examples (màglà, tèrè, físhí, kóɗóm, túlúm); no mention of stress or accent anywhere (a full-text search for stress/accent/Akzent/Betonung: no hits).

sources.citation: Leger, Rudolf. 2014. Some observations on typological features in languages of the Bole-Tangale group. In A. Storch, J. Harnischfeger & R. Leger (eds.), Fading Delimitations (Topics in Interdisciplinary African Studies 34), 229-261. Cologne: Köppe.
